episode_title: Turn Imposter Syndrome Into Growth with Victoria Jenn Rodriguez | Pivot to Profit

real_qa.q: How did Victoria Jen Rodriguez transition from Wall Street to entrepreneurship after working at Lehman Brothers?
real_qa.r: After working at Lehman Brothers in operations and sales and trading for two years, and remaining in corporate for 15 years total, Rodriguez was laid off nine years ago. While interviewing for other corporate positions, she kept reaching final rounds but couldn't close the deals. She took this as a sign from God and decided to start her own business. She never returned to corporate, and nine years later has built a thriving consulting practice.
real_qa.requete: Victoria Jen Rodriguez Lehman Brothers to entrepreneurship

real_qa.q: What was Victoria Jen Rodriguez's first consulting client and how much did she earn?
real_qa.r: In her first year of starting her consulting business, Rodriguez secured BlackRock, the top asset manager in the world, as her first consulting client. She made more money on that first big consulting opportunity than she had made in her entire career. She had started by doing resumes for $300 each, but after meeting someone at a conference who made $100,000 in two months, she pivoted to high-level consulting.
real_qa.requete: BlackRock Victoria Jen Rodriguez first consulting client

real_qa.q: How does Victoria Jen Rodriguez define imposter syndrome and what does it signal?
real_qa.r: Rodriguez defines imposter syndrome as a gift and a blessing because it is a signal that you are expanding, entering new environments, coloring outside the lines, and doing something you have never done before. She emphasizes that it is a very normal human experience, noting that Oprah, Jennifer Lopez, and Tony Robbins have all said they experience imposter syndrome even at the peak of their careers because they are always doing something new.

real_qa.q: What is the Dare to Leap Academy and who does it serve?
real_qa.r: Dare to Leap Academy is a curriculum-based program that works with women who are thinking about entrepreneurship but don't know where to start. The academy teaches women how to decide what type of business to start, covers business fundamentals like taxes and LLC versus S-Corp structures, marketing, sales, and how to secure corporate and government contracts. Rodriguez also works with women in transition who are on the brink of reinvention and need to let go of old identities that no longer serve them.
real_qa.requete: Dare to Leap Academy women entrepreneurship curriculum

real_qa.q: What is Victoria Jen Rodriguez's current focus on retreats and geographic expansion?
real_qa.r: Rodriguez recently launched a new pillar in her business focused on hosting retreats for groups of women in more intimate settings instead of large conferences. She has shifted from hosting conferences with 500 people to smaller retreat groups where she can work with people at a deeper level. Her next retreat is coming up in Morocco, and she plans to host retreats all around the world as part of her heart-led, purpose-driven work.
real_qa.requete: Victoria Jen Rodriguez retreats Morocco women

guest.bio_context: Victoria Jen Rodriguez has more than two decades of experience and has trained over 20,000 leaders and entrepreneurs. She has worked with major brands including Amazon, Coca-Cola, and Walmart. Her podcast Banking on Cultura has generated more than 25 million impressions. She transitioned from Wall Street (Lehman Brothers, sales and trading) and 15 years in corporate leadership and development roles to founding her consulting business nine years ago.
